blurb.en: Square brackets with one number give you a character; with colons they give you a piece - and the two react very differently to a position that is not there.
blurb.zh: 方括号里一个数，拿到的是一个字符；带冒号，拿到的是一段——而这两种写法碰到不存在的位置时，反应截然不同。

en: Positions start at 0 from the left and at -1 from the right, so every character has two names: in "Python" the h is both 3 and -3. Negative positions are not a trick; they are how you reach the end of a string without first asking how long it is.

A slice has up to three parts, start:stop:step, and the stop is never included. That one rule is why a piece from 0 to 2 has exactly 2 characters, and why cutting at the same position twice - once as a stop, once as a start - splits a string with nothing lost and nothing repeated. Leave a part out and Python fills in the natural default: the beginning, the end, a step of 1.

The last two lines of output are the real lesson. A slice that runs past the end is quietly trimmed to what exists, and one that starts past the end is simply empty. A single index past the end is an IndexError. Slicing asks for "whatever is in this range"; indexing insists that one particular character exists.
The try / except lines are only there so the program survives the error and prints its message; how they work belongs to the Files and Errors page, not this one.
zh: 位置从左数从 0 开始，从右数从 -1 开始，所以每个字符都有两个名字："Python" 里的 h 既是 3 也是 -3。负数下标不是花招，它让你不必先问字符串有多长，就能够到末尾。
切片最多三段：start:stop:step，而且终点永远不包含在内。就是这一条规矩，让 0 到 2 的那一段恰好 2 个字符；也让你在同一个位置切两次——一次当终点、一次当起点——把字符串分成两半时既不丢字也不重字。某一段不写，Python 就补上自然的默认值：开头、末尾、步长 1。
输出的最后两行才是真正要学的。切片越过末尾，会被悄悄截到实际存在的部分；起点就在末尾之外的切片，干脆是空串。而单个下标越界，是 IndexError。切片问的是「这个范围里有什么」；下标坚持要那一个字符必须存在。
try / except 那几行只是为了让程序挨过这个错误、把报错信息打印出来；它们怎么工作是「文件与异常」那一页的事，这里不讲。

lineNotes.en: Start at 1 to skip the first character; stop at -1, which is excluded, to drop the last. The same slice works for a word of any length.
lineNotes.zh: 从 1 开始，跳过第一个字符；停在 -1——它不被包含——于是去掉最后一个。任何长度的单词都用这同一个切片。

lineNotes.en: No error on either: 100 is trimmed to the real end, and a start past the end gives an empty string. repr() makes the empty string visible as ''.
lineNotes.zh: 两个都不报错：100 被截到真正的末尾，起点在末尾之外得到空串。repr() 让空串显示成 ''，看得见。

lineNotes.en: The same position that was harmless inside a slice is an IndexError on its own.
lineNotes.zh: 同一个位置，放进切片里毫无问题，单独当下标就是 IndexError。

blurb.en: You cannot change a character inside a string. Every "change" builds a new string, and the old one is left exactly as it was.
blurb.zh: 字符串里的字符改不了。每一次「修改」都是造一个新串，旧的原封不动。

en: Assigning to name[0] is a TypeError, not a silent no-op: a str has no way to change its own contents. That is a design decision, and it buys something - a string you pass to a function comes back unchanged, always, because nothing is able to change it.

So every string operation that looks like a change is really a construction. upper(), replace() and slicing all return a new string. If you want to keep the result you must assign it to a name; call greeting.replace(...) on a line of its own and the new string is built and immediately thrown away. This is the most common string bug there is.

The last four lines show the same fact from the other side. greeting = greeting + "!" does not change the string that before refers to; it builds a new string and moves the name greeting onto it. before still shows the old text, because the old string never changed.
The try / except lines are only there so the program survives the error and prints its message; how they work belongs to the Files and Errors page, not this one.
zh: 给 name[0] 赋值是 TypeError，不是悄无声息地什么也不做：str 根本没有改自己内容的办法。这是有意的设计，换来的好处是：你把一个字符串交给函数，它回来时一定没变——因为谁也改不了它。
所以每个看起来像「修改」的字符串操作，其实都是在「造」。upper()、replace()、切片，交回的都是新串。想留下结果就必须赋给一个名字；把 greeting.replace(...) 单独写成一行，新串造出来就立刻被扔掉了。这是字符串最常见的一个 bug。
最后四行从另一面说同一件事。greeting = greeting + "!" 并没有改 before 指着的那个串；它造了一个新串，再把 greeting 这个名字挪过去。before 显示的仍是旧文字，因为旧串从来没变过。
try / except 那几行只是为了让程序挨过这个错误、把报错信息打印出来；它们怎么工作是「文件与异常」那一页的事，这里不讲。

lineNotes.en: This line never completes: Python raises TypeError before anything is stored, so name is still all lower case two lines later.
lineNotes.zh: 这一行永远做不完：什么都还没存进去，Python 就抛了 TypeError，所以两行之后 name 仍然全是小写。

lineNotes.en: The capital-letter fix, done the only way strings allow: build a new string out of pieces of the old one.
lineNotes.zh: 把首字母改大写，用的是字符串唯一允许的做法：拿旧串的几段拼出一个新串。

lineNotes.en: Everything before the position, the new character, everything after it. The + 1 is what skips the character being replaced.
lineNotes.zh: 位置之前的全部、新字符、位置之后的全部。+ 1 正是跳过被替换掉的那个字符的那一步。

blurb.en: Tidy, search, test and count: the dozen methods that cover most of what programs do with text, each shown once with its result.
blurb.zh: 整理、查找、判断、计数：程序处理文本时大部分时候用到的那十来个方法，每个演示一次、配上结果。

en: strip() removes whitespace from both ends only - the spaces between words stay. lower(), upper() and title() change case, and because strings are immutable each of them hands back a new string, which is why they can be chained: raw.strip() is a string, so you can call another method on it straight away.

find() and index() both tell you where a substring starts, and differ only when it is missing: find() returns -1, index() raises ValueError. Use find() when "not there" is an ordinary answer you will test for; use index() when it would mean something has gone wrong. Watch out for -1 in particular: it is also a valid index (the last character), so forgetting to test for it gives a wrong answer rather than a crash.

count() counts non-overlapping matches, which is why "banana" contains "an" twice. The is-methods ask a question about every character at once: isdigit() is False for "20.5" and "-7" because the point and the minus sign are not digits, and every is-method returns False for the empty string. That last detail is why is_pin also checks the length rather than trusting isdigit() alone.
The try / except lines are only there so the program survives the error and prints its message; how they work belongs to the Files and Errors page, not this one.
zh: strip() 只去掉两头的空白——词与词之间的空格留着。lower()、upper()、title() 改大小写；字符串不可变，所以它们交回的都是新串，也正因为如此它们才能串起来：raw.strip() 本身就是个字符串，可以直接接着调下一个方法。
find() 和 index() 都告诉你子串从哪里开始，只在找不到时不同：find() 交回 -1，index() 抛 ValueError。「找不到」是你本来就要判断的正常结果时用 find()；找不到就意味着出了错时用 index()。尤其要当心 -1：它同时也是一个合法下标（最后一个字符），忘了判断它，得到的是一个错答案而不是一次崩溃。
count() 数的是互不重叠的匹配，所以 "banana" 里 "an" 只算两次。is 开头的方法一次问遍每个字符："20.5" 和 "-7" 的 isdigit() 是 False，因为小数点和负号不是数字；而且每个 is 方法对空串都交回 False。最后这个细节，正是 is_pin 还要另外检查长度、不单信 isdigit() 的原因。
try / except 那几行只是为了让程序挨过这个错误、把报错信息打印出来；它们怎么工作是「文件与异常」那一页的事，这里不讲。

lineNotes.en: 6 is where the underscore starts; -1 means not found. Nothing is raised.
lineNotes.zh: 6 是下划线开始的位置；-1 表示没找到。不抛任何错。

lineNotes.en: Same search as find("z") above, but a missing substring is an error here.
lineNotes.zh: 和上面的 find("z") 是同一次查找，但在这里找不到就是错误。

lineNotes.en: Methods work on a string literal directly - no variable needed.
lineNotes.zh: 方法可以直接在字符串字面量上调用，不需要先存进变量。

blurb.en: split() turns one string into a list of pieces; join() turns a list of strings back into one. The pair is how programs take text apart and put it back together.
blurb.zh: split() 把一个字符串变成一列片段；join() 把一列字符串拼回一个。程序拆开文本、再拼回去，靠的就是这一对。

en: split() with no argument and split(" ") look alike and are not. With no argument Python splits on any run of whitespace and drops empty pieces, so leading, trailing and repeated spaces all disappear. With " " it cuts at every single space, and two spaces in a row leave an empty string between them. The two lines of output for the same text show the difference.

The second argument to split() is the most cuts to make. It matters whenever the last field may itself contain the separator: a time like 12:30:05 after a key must be cut once, not three times, or the unpacking into key and value fails.

join() reads backwards at first: it is called on the separator, and the list goes in the brackets. That is because the separator is the only thing that is always a string - the list could hold anything. Every item must already be a string, though; joining a list of numbers raises TypeError, so convert them first.
zh: 不带实参的 split() 和 split(" ") 看起来像，其实不一样。不带实参时，Python 按任意长度的空白切，并丢掉空片段，所以开头、末尾和连续的空格统统消失。带 " " 时它在每一个空格处都切一刀，两个空格挨着就会在中间留下一个空串。同一段文字的那两行输出，把差别摆在眼前。
split() 的第二个实参是最多切几刀。只要最后一个字段本身可能含有分隔符，它就要紧：键后面跟着 12:30:05 这样的时间，只能切一刀，不能切三刀，否则解包给 key 和 value 时就失败。
join() 一开始读起来是反的：它是在分隔符上调用的，列表放在括号里。原因是分隔符是唯一一个「一定是字符串」的东西——列表里可以装任何东西。不过列表里每一项都必须已经是字符串；拿一列数字去 join 会抛 TypeError，得先转换。

lineNotes.en: Count the empty strings: one for each extra space at the start, between words and at the end.
lineNotes.zh: 数一数里面的空串：开头、词与词之间、末尾，每多出一个空格就多一个。

lineNotes.en: Two cuts, three pieces - the rest of the line stays together in the last one.
lineNotes.zh: 切两刀，得三段——剩下的部分整个留在最后一段里。

lineNotes.en: An empty separator glues the pieces with nothing between them.
lineNotes.zh: 分隔符是空串，片段之间就什么都不夹，直接粘在一起。

blurb.en: A backslash inside a string starts a two-character code for one character. Raw strings switch that off, and repr() shows you which is which.
blurb.zh: 字符串里的反斜杠开启一个「两个字符代表一个字符」的代码。原始字符串把它关掉，而 repr() 让你看清哪个是哪个。

en: In source code \n is two characters you type, but in the string it is one character: a newline. The same goes for \t (a tab), \\ (one backslash) and \" (a double quote that does not end the string). len() counts the characters in the string, not the keystrokes in your source, which is why "first\nsecond" has length 12.

print() shows a string the way a reader sees it: the newline breaks the line and the tab jumps to a column. repr() shows it the way you would type it back into Python, with the escapes written out and quotes around it. When a string looks wrong, print its repr() - hidden newlines, tabs and trailing spaces all become visible.

A raw string, written with an r in front, treats a backslash as an ordinary character. That makes it the natural way to write Windows paths and, later, regular expressions. The last lines show the trap it saves you from: in an ordinary string a path containing \t and \n silently turns into a tab and a newline - no error, just a shorter, wrong string with no backslashes left in it.
zh: 源码里的 \n 是你敲的两个字符，但在字符串里它是一个字符：换行符。\t（制表符）、\\（一个反斜杠）、\"（一个不结束字符串的双引号）也一样。len() 数的是字符串里的字符，不是你在源码里敲的键数，所以 "first\nsecond" 的长度是 12。
print() 按读者看到的样子显示字符串：换行符真的换行，制表符跳到下一栏。repr() 按你要把它敲回 Python 的样子显示：转义写出来，外面加上引号。一个字符串看着不对劲时，打印它的 repr()——藏着的换行、制表符、行尾空格统统现形。
原始字符串前面带一个 r，把反斜杠当普通字符。所以写 Windows 路径（以后还有正则表达式）时，它是最自然的写法。最后几行展示的正是它帮你躲开的陷阱：在普通字符串里，路径中的 \t 和 \n 会悄悄变成制表符和换行符——不报错，只是得到一个更短的、错的、一个反斜杠都不剩的字符串。

lineNotes.en: repr() writes the newline back as \n; len() counts it as the single character it really is.
lineNotes.zh: repr() 把换行符写回成 \n；len() 把它按实际的一个字符来数。

lineNotes.en: repr() picks double quotes for a string containing an apostrophe, so no escape is needed; the backslash string has length 1 even though repr() shows two backslashes.
lineNotes.zh: 字符串里有撇号时，repr() 会改用双引号包起来，就不必转义；反斜杠那个串长度是 1，尽管 repr() 显示了两个反斜杠。

lineNotes.en: No r and no doubled backslashes: \t becomes a tab and \n a newline. Python gives no warning.
lineNotes.zh: 没有 r，反斜杠也没有双写：\t 变成了制表符、\n 变成了换行符。Python 不会提醒你。

blurb.en: The whole reversal in one slice, with nothing but a negative step.
blurb.zh: 整个反转就是一个切片，只靠一个负的步长。

en: A negative step walks the string from right to left. When the step is negative, the defaults for the empty start and stop flip as well: start means the last character and stop means past the first one, so leaving both out covers the whole string backwards.

Put this next to reverse-string-loop. The loop spells out what reversing is - take each character and put it in front - while the slice states the result and lets Python do the walking. Both give the same answer for every string, including the empty one; the slice is what you would write in practice, the loop is what an exam asks you to be able to explain.
zh: 负的步长让切片从右往左走。步长为负时，起点和终点留空时的默认值也跟着翻过来：起点表示最后一个字符，终点表示走过第一个字符为止——所以两个都不写，就是把整个字符串倒着走一遍。
把它和 reverse-string-loop 并排看。循环把「反转」是什么一步步写出来——拿出每个字符、放到前面；切片只说出结果，让 Python 去走。两者对任何字符串（包括空串）给出同样的答案；实际写程序时用切片，卷子要你讲得出来的是循环。

lineNotes.en: Start and stop are empty, the step is -1: the whole string, one character at a time, from the right.
lineNotes.zh: 起点、终点留空，步长 -1：整个字符串，从右边开始，一次一个字符。

blurb.en: Build the reversed string yourself, putting each character in front of the ones already collected.
blurb.zh: 自己动手造出反转后的字符串：每个字符都放到已经收集到的那些前面。

en: The accumulator pattern with one twist. result starts empty, the loop visits the characters left to right, and each one is placed in front of what has been built so far. After s, t, r the result reads rts: the first character read ends up last.

The order of the + is the whole algorithm. Put ch on the right instead and you add each character to the end, which rebuilds the original string - a program that runs, prints something plausible, and is wrong. When a loop result looks suspiciously like its input, check which side you are adding on.
Each step builds a brand-new string, because strings are immutable. For the short strings here that costs nothing; the slice in reverse-string-slice is still the version you would use in real code.
zh: 累加器模式加一个小变化。result 从空串开始，循环从左到右访问每个字符，每个都放到已经造好的那部分前面。读过 s、t、r 之后，result 是 rts：先读到的字符落在最后。
+ 两边的顺序就是整个算法。把 ch 放到右边，就变成每个字符接到末尾，造出来的还是原来那个串——程序能跑、打印的东西看着像回事、却是错的。循环的结果可疑地像输入时，查一查你是往哪一边加。
字符串不可变，所以每一步都造了一个全新的串。对这里的短串来说毫无代价；实际代码里用的仍然是 reverse-string-slice 那个切片。

lineNotes.en: ch on the left: the character just read goes in front of everything collected so far.
lineNotes.zh: ch 在左边：刚读到的字符放在已经收集到的全部前面。

blurb.en: Clean the phrase first, then compare it with its reverse. The cleaning is where all the real decisions are.
blurb.zh: 先把短语规整干净，再和它的反转比。真正要拿主意的地方全在规整那一步。

en: "A man, a plan, a canal: Panama!" is a palindrome only after you decide what does not count: spaces, punctuation and the difference between capital and small letters. clean() makes those decisions in one place, so is_palindrome() can be a single honest comparison.

isalnum() is True for letters and digits and False for everything else, which is exactly the set that should survive. Lower-casing each kept character means R and r compare equal. Splitting the work into two functions also makes the output easier to trust: the program prints the cleaned string next to the verdict, so you can see what was actually compared.

The empty string counts as a palindrome - it reads the same both ways. A phrase with no letters or digits at all cleans down to the empty string and so is also reported as a palindrome; if that is not what you want, it is a rule you have to add, not something the comparison will decide for you.
zh: "A man, a plan, a canal: Panama!" 只有在你先决定「哪些不算」之后才是回文：空格、标点、大小写的差别。clean() 把这些决定集中在一处做完，is_palindrome() 就只剩一个老老实实的比较。
isalnum() 对字母和数字为 True、对其他一切为 False，正好就是该留下来的那一类。留下的字符一律转小写，R 和 r 就比得相等。把活拆成两个函数，也让输出更可信：程序在判定旁边打印规整后的串，你看得见实际比较的到底是什么。
空串算回文——正读反读都一样。一个一个字母数字都没有的短语，规整之后就是空串，所以也会被判成回文；如果这不是你想要的，那是一条要你自己加上的规则，比较本身不会替你决定。

lineNotes.en: Clean once and keep the result: the comparison below uses it twice.
lineNotes.zh: 只规整一次，把结果存下来：下面的比较要用它两次。

lineNotes.en: A comparison is already True or False, so it is returned directly - no if needed.
lineNotes.zh: 比较的结果本身就是 True 或 False，所以直接交回去，不需要 if。

blurb.en: Turn letters into numbers with ord(), shift them, wrap round with % 26, and turn them back with chr(). Everything that is not a letter passes through untouched.
blurb.zh: 用 ord() 把字母变成数，平移，用 % 26 绕回来，再用 chr() 变回字母。不是字母的一律原样通过。

en: ord() gives the code number of a character and chr() turns a code back into a character. Codes for a to z are consecutive (97 to 122), and so are A to Z (65 to 90), which is what makes arithmetic on letters possible. The trick is to work with the position inside the alphabet, 0 to 25, rather than the raw code: subtract the code of the first letter, shift, then add it back.

% 26 is what makes z wrap round to c with a key of 3. In Python the result of % always has the sign of the divisor, so a negative position also wraps into 0 to 25 - which is why caesar(secret, -3) decrypts, and why a key of 29 behaves exactly like a key of 3.

shift_char() handles upper and lower case separately by picking a different base, and returns anything else unchanged. Keeping case and punctuation is what makes the output readable as a disguised sentence rather than a jumble, and it is a rule exam questions like to state explicitly.
zh: ord() 给出一个字符的编码，chr() 把编码变回字符。a 到 z 的编码是连续的（97 到 122），A 到 Z 也是（65 到 90），这才让对字母做算术成为可能。窍门是在字母表里的位置（0 到 25）上算，而不是直接在编码上算：先减去第一个字母的编码，平移，再加回去。
密钥是 3 时 z 能绕回 c，靠的是 % 26。Python 里 % 的结果符号永远跟除数一致，所以负的位置也会绕回 0 到 25——这就是 caesar(secret, -3) 能解密、密钥 29 与密钥 3 效果完全相同的原因。
shift_char() 靠选不同的 base 分别处理大写和小写，其他字符原样交回。保留大小写与标点，输出读起来才像一句伪装过的话而不是一团乱码；这也是考题喜欢明确写出来的一条规则。

lineNotes.en: A chained comparison: ch is at least a and at most z. Strings compare by character code.
lineNotes.zh: 连写比较：ch 不小于 a、也不大于 z。字符串之间按字符编码比较。

lineNotes.en: 29 wraps to the same shift as 3; -1 moves a back round to z.
lineNotes.zh: 29 绕回来与平移 3 相同；-1 把 a 往回绕到 z。

run.expect:
Khoor, Zruog!
Hello, World!
abc ABC
def zab
97 65 25 d

blurb.en: Read the bits left to right, and each time double what you have and add the new bit. No powers of 2 needed.
blurb.zh: 从左到右读每一位，每次把已有的翻倍、再加上新的一位。用不着 2 的幂。

en: The method you learn on paper writes place values under the bits - 128, 64, 32 and so on - and adds up the ones under a 1. That needs the length of the string before you start. Reading left to right and doubling does not: every time a new bit arrives, all the bits already read move one place to the left, which in binary means their value doubles.

Trace 101 by hand: start at 0; read 1, value is 0 * 2 + 1 = 1; read 0, value is 1 * 2 + 0 = 2; read 1, value is 2 * 2 + 1 = 5. The same loop works in any base - change the 2 to a 10 and it turns the characters of "372" into the number 372.
bit is a character, "0" or "1", not a number, so it must go through int() before it can be added. Leading zeros cost nothing: 00101 doubles 0 twice before anything happens and still gives 5.
zh: 纸上学的办法是在每一位下面写出位权——128、64、32……——再把 1 底下的加起来。那得先知道这串有多长。从左往右读、每次翻倍就不用：每来一位新的，之前读到的所有位都往左挪一格，在二进制里就是值翻倍。
手算一遍 101：从 0 开始；读到 1，值是 0 * 2 + 1 = 1；读到 0，值是 1 * 2 + 0 = 2；读到 1，值是 2 * 2 + 1 = 5。同一个循环适用于任何进制——把 2 换成 10，它就把 "372" 这几个字符变成数 372。
bit 是字符 "0" 或 "1"，不是数，所以要先过一遍 int() 才能相加。前导零毫无代价：00101 先把 0 翻倍两次，什么都没发生，结果仍是 5。

lineNotes.en: Nothing read yet, so the value so far is 0 - and 0 doubled is still 0, so the first bit lands correctly.
lineNotes.zh: 还一位都没读，目前的值是 0——0 翻倍还是 0，所以第一位能正确落位。

title.en: Binary to Denary: int() and bin()
title.zh: 二进制转十进制：int() 与 bin()

blurb.en: The built-ins do both directions: int() with a base reads binary, bin() writes it - with a 0b prefix you usually cut off.
blurb.zh: 内置函数两个方向都包了：带进制的 int() 读二进制，bin() 写二进制——带着一个通常要切掉的 0b 前缀。

en: int() with one argument reads denary, which is why int("101") is one hundred and one. Give it a second argument and it reads that base instead: 2 for binary, 16 for hexadecimal. The characters must be valid for the base - int("102", 2) is a ValueError.

bin() goes the other way and returns a string, not a number, starting with 0b. That prefix is how Python writes binary literals in code, and int() with base 2 accepts it, but for display you normally slice it off.

Compare this with binary-to-denary-loop: same inputs, same outputs. In your own programs use the built-ins; in an exam you are usually asked to show the algorithm, which is what the loop version is for.
zh: 只给一个实参时 int() 按十进制读，所以 int("101") 是一百零一。给它第二个实参，它就按那个进制读：2 是二进制，16 是十六进制。字符必须在那个进制里合法——int("102", 2) 是 ValueError。
bin() 走相反的方向，交回的是字符串而不是数，开头是 0b。这个前缀是 Python 在代码里写二进制字面量的方式，按 2 进制读的 int() 也认它；但用来显示时通常要切掉。
拿它和 binary-to-denary-loop 对照：同样的输入、同样的输出。自己写程序时用内置函数；考试通常要你把算法写出来，那正是循环版存在的理由。

lineNotes.en: bin() keeps the 0b prefix; to_binary() cuts it off.
lineNotes.zh: bin() 带着 0b 前缀；to_binary() 把它切掉了。

lineNotes.en: A round trip loses the leading zeros: they carry no value, so nothing remembers them.
lineNotes.zh: 转过去再转回来，前导零没了：它们不带任何值，所以没有东西记得它们。

blurb.en: One pass over the characters sets a flag for each kind found; then each rule is checked in turn, and every rule that fails is reported, not just the first.
blurb.zh: 遍历一次字符，每发现一类就立一个标志；然后逐条检查规则，把每一条没通过的都报出来，而不只是第一条。

en: The loop does not decide anything about the password. It only records facts - has an upper-case letter been seen, a lower-case one, a digit - in three variables that start False and can only ever be switched to True. The decisions come afterwards, once all the facts are in.

Returning a list of every broken rule, rather than True or False, is what a real sign-up form needs: telling someone "invalid password" makes them guess, telling them exactly which rules failed does not. An empty list means the password passed, and an empty list is falsy, which is why the demo block can test it with a plain if.

The rules are separate if statements, not an elif chain, because they are independent: a password can be too short and have no digit at the same time. Inside the loop, though, elif is correct - one character cannot be upper case, lower case and a digit at once.
zh: 循环不对密码下任何结论。它只记录事实——见没见过大写字母、小写字母、数字——记在三个从 False 开始、只可能被改成 True 的变量里。结论在之后下，等所有事实都收齐了再说。
交回一列没通过的规则而不是 True 或 False，才是真正的注册表单需要的：只告诉对方「密码无效」，他得去猜；把没通过的规则一条条列出来，就不用猜。空列表表示通过，而空列表的真值为假，所以演示块里用一个普通的 if 就能判断。
规则是一条条独立的 if，不是 elif 链，因为它们互不相干：一个密码可以既太短又没有数字。而循环里面用 elif 是对的——一个字符不可能同时是大写、小写和数字。

lineNotes.en: Every flag starts False: nothing has been seen yet.
lineNotes.zh: 每个标志都从 False 开始：什么都还没见到。

lineNotes.en: Start with no failures and append one description per broken rule.
lineNotes.zh: 从没有失败开始，每违反一条规则就追加一条说明。

lineNotes.en: An empty list counts as False, so this branch runs only when at least one rule failed.
lineNotes.zh: 空列表算假，所以只有至少一条规则没通过时才走这一支。

run.expect:
password fails: an upper-case letter, a digit
Passw0rd is OK
short1A fails: at least 8 characters
ALL CAPS 123 fails: a lower-case letter, no spaces
Tr0ub4dor&3 is OK
